s: family is regulated regulated (in such a state of concord and harmony)

s: parents have complacence entire (in such a state of things)

s: the way of the superior man is compared to ascending a height
q: The way of the superior man may be compared to what takes place in traveling, when to go to a distance we must first traverse the space that is near, and in ascending a height, when we must begin from the lower ground.

s: Book of Poetry contains union with wife and children
q: It is said in the Book of Poetry, "Happy union with wife and children is like the music of lutes and harps.

s: spiritual beings display powers (abundantly)
q: How abundantly do spiritual beings display the powers that belong to them!

s: Book of Poetry contains approaches of the spirits (a saying about them)
q: It is said in the Book of Poetry, 'The approaches of the spirits, you cannot surmise; and can you treat them with indifference?'

s: sincerity has outgoings manifestness (impossible to repress)

s: powers belong to spiritual beings
q: the powers that belong to them

s: people engage in fasting and purification (in preparation for sacrifices)

s: people attend sacrifices (after fasting and purification)
q: in order to attend at their sacrifices

s: spiritual beings are over worshippers (over their heads and on their right and left, like overflowing water)

s: duke of Chau completes the virtuous course of Wan and Wu
q: the duke of Chau completed the virtuous course of Wan and Wu.

s: duke of Chau carries title of king to King Chi
q: He carried up the title of king to T'ai and Chi, and sacrificed to all the former dukes above them with the royal ceremonies.

s: duke of Chau sacrifices to the former dukes (with the royal ceremonies)
q: He carried up the title of king to T'ai and Chi, and sacrificed to all the former dukes above them with the royal ceremonies.

s: duke of Chau extends rule to princes of the kingdom
q: And this rule he extended to the princes of the kingdom, the great officers, the scholars, and the common people.

q: And this rule he extended to the princes of the kingdom, the great officers, the scholars, and the common people.

q: And this rule he extended to the princes of the kingdom, the great officers, the scholars, and the common people.

s: mourning extends to Son of Heaven (for three years)

s: mourning allows no difference between noble and mean (for a father or mother)
q: In the mourning for a father or mother, he allowed no difference between the noble and the mean.

s: King Wan has no cause for grief none
q: It is only King Wan of whom it can be said that he had no cause for grief!

s: King Chi lays foundations of King Wan's dignity
q: His father laid the foundations of his dignity, and his son transmitted it.

s: King Wu has father King Chi
q: His father was King Chi, and his son was King Wu.

s: King Wu continues the enterprise of King T'ai, King Chi, and King Wan
q: King Wu continued the enterprise of King T'ai, King Chi, and King Wan.

s: King Wu has dignity throne
q: His dignity was the royal throne.

s: King Wu has riches the possession of all within the four seas

q: He offered his sacrifices in his ancestral temple, and his descendants maintained the sacrifices to himself.

s: filial piety is a skillful carrying out of the wishes of forefathers (now seen in)

s: filial piety carries forward undertakings (skillfully; those of forefathers)
q: "Now filial piety is seen in the skillful carrying out of the wishes of our forefathers, and the skillful carrying forward of their undertakings.

q: By the arrangement of the services, they made a distinction of talents and worth.

s: ancestral temple serves ancestors (through ceremonies of sacrifice)

q: The Duke Ai asked about government.
